Apple's major September launch event is just around the corner, at which three brand-new iPhone models will be unveiled: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Below is a roundup of the highlights the industry is looking forward to.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will succeed Apple's popular 17 Pro lineup.

Rumoured new features include:

  • A20 Pro chip with comprehensive boosts in performance and efficiency
  • Major camera upgrades, including a variable aperture design for the main lens
  • Dynamic Island shrunk by 35%, giving the design a more modern look
  • New colour options, kicking off with a bold burgundy
  • The best battery life ever, with the iPhone 18 Pro Max seeing particularly significant improvements
  • Redesigned Camera Control button
  • Equipped with Apple's in-house C2 cellular modem
  • New satellite communication features, including 5G support

The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to see a higher starting price. Outside estimates put it at around US$1,399, but my own calculations put it closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is rumoured to be Apple's first folding iPhone, with an expected price tag exceeding US$2,000, carving out an entirely new premium market position.

The folding design makes the iPhone Ultra the most groundbreaking model Apple has ever released. The device uses a wide book-style fold, with an outer display of around 5.4 inches and an inner display of 7.8 inches, similar in size to the iPad mini.

The body materials are expected to mirror those of the iPhone Air, paired with a titanium frame for a cleaner, more stylish look.

The iPhone Ultra will feature two rear cameras (main and ultra-wide) along with two front cameras, one for each display. Authentication will switch from Face ID to Touch ID.

Software will be the biggest highlight of this device. The accompanying iOS 27 supports side-by-side multitasking for apps and adaptive landscape layouts, perfectly complementing the new form factor.

Performance is expected to be on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, also using the A20 Pro chip, with a vapour chamber cooling system and the C2 modem.

Where are the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2?

As usual, Apple's September event typically also sees the launch of the new entry-level iPhone 18 and the successor to the iPhone Air.

However, reports suggest Apple will significantly reshuffle its autumn product lineup this year, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to early 2027.

It remains unclear whether this is purely a strategic move or forced by the ongoing memory chip shortage. Either way, the absence of more affordable models means this autumn's iPhone lineup will focus its firepower on the premium market.
